title: Teacher's question cards: Why do some farmers grow food only for their families? How does fair trade help farmers? Why is crop rotation sustainable?
subject: English
source: Written for english/y5 lesson 75 (Teacher's question cards: Why do some farmers grow food only for their families? How does fair trade help farmers? Why is crop rotation sustainable?)
intro: Lesson 75: Researching and planning an explanation text. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

cards: Why do some farmers grow food only for their families?
How does fair trade help farmers?
blocks.task: choose one question to research and explain.

panels.title: Subsistence farming
points: Farmers grow food mainly to feed their own families
Plots are often small, with little money for seeds or machines
Farms may be far from markets, with poor roads

panels.title: Fair trade
points: Farmers are paid a fair minimum price for crops such as cocoa, coffee and bananas
An extra payment (a premium) helps the community, for example with wells or schools
Products carry a Fairtrade mark so shoppers can choose them

panels.title: Crop rotation
points: Different crops are grown in a field each year
Beans and peas put nitrogen back into the soil
Changing crops stops pests and diseases building up, so less spray is needed

model.title: Why Do Some Farmers Grow Food Only for Their Families?

parts.text: Introduction: what subsistence farming is and where it happens
Paragraph 1 (cause): small plots and little money for seeds or machines
Paragraph 2 (cause): far from markets, poor roads
Paragraph 3 (effect): food grown is eaten; little left to sell
Conclusion: how fair trade and cooperatives can help

keywords.def: writing that explains how or why something happens
steps that follow sensibly from one to the next
a title that asks what the text will answer: Why do...?

questions.q: Write a question title for fair trade
questions.a: For example: How Does Fair Trade Help Farmers?

questions.q: Put in order: effects, introduction, causes
Note one fact from your fact sheet
Core: choose a question, research it and plan 3 linked paragraphs
questions.a: A plan with a question title, introduction, three paragraphs and links

questions.q: Extend: plan the connective at the start of each paragraph
Stretch: plan a labelled diagram or flow chart

questions.a: B) What subsistence farming is. Readers need to know what it is before the causes and solutions.
